who: two field hands waiting for the dew to burn off

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Grass is soaking. Cut it now and it rots in the cock.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So we stand here like herons till the sun's up.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Herons get paid better. They eat what they catch.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Mist on the low meadow again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: My gran said mist at dawn means the Blight's breathing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Your gran said that about everything. Even the cat.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can't we start? Dew or no dew, I'm hungry.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wet hay heats and burns the rick. Then we're all hungry.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fine. I'll chew a grass stem and pretend it's bread.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Dew never lifts in Reedwatch. The whole fen's a dew.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we'll wait till Lammas, and {steward} can mow it himself.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He'd count the blades first, to tax them.

who: two shepherds driving the flock into the fold

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Count them through the gate. I make it forty-one.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Forty. The lame ewe's dragging at the back.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Get her in. The wolves can count to one.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Heard the wolves had Dunworth's folds again last night.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Six ewes. Forest Charter says only the lord's hunt may kill them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then the lord can come and sit up with my lambs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wynstead lost another ram. Greybeard won't break his own charter.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Too holy to hunt wolves, too frightened to ride out.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pray harder, he says. Prayers don't bark.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Whitden pays the Thornbacks and the Red Crows both for its sheep.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Cheapest peace in the realm, they say.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Cheap till both bands want the same fat wether.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hurdles tied? Every one?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Tied twice. And the dog's on the windward side.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good. I'm sleeping in the fold tonight. Wake me if he growls.

who: two dairy hands at the cows

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hold her tail, she's flicking me in the eye.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: She knows you've cold hands. Warm them first.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Warm them where? The only warm thing here is her.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Half a pail. She's drying off early.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Grass is thin. Thin grass, thin milk.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Thin cheese, then, and thin words from the mistress.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say Kirkden's goats give grey milk since the Blight came through.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Grey milk. I'd not feed that to a pig.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The Sunward folk would bottle it and sell it as a wonder.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Two full churns before the bell. Good butter week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Put some by. Fat weeks don't last.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You'd find a shadow in a sunbeam, you would.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Last of the good hay. After this it's straw and hope.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Cut the straw with a bit of pease haulm. They'll eat it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They'll eat it. They won't thank us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {steward} wants two cows sold before winter.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fewer mouths in the byre. Fewer calves in spring, too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He never thinks past the next tally, that one.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Old Bramble's off her feed.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Give her a warm mash with a fistful of salt.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Salt costs. She'd better be grateful.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sack of what is this? It weighs like a sin.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Salt, from Sunward. Mind it doesn't split.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: If it splits I'm licking the road clean.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Two more sacks to the chandler, then we eat.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You said that four sacks ago.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And I meant it every time.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My back's gone, and the pay's a heel of bread.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Better than nothing. The outlaws pay in meat, I hear.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And a rope at the end of it. I'll take the bread.

who: two quarrymen at the stone face

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Drive the wedge along the bed, not across it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I know how stone breaks. I've broken more than you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You've broken more toes than stone.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wet the wedges overnight?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Swelled tight. Face should split by noon.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then stand clear of it. Last split took Hal's foot.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Heard a face fell at another quarry. Stone's dear now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Dear stone means we're worth something for once.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Tell that to the master. He's not raised our pay.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Best stone in the realm, this. Grey as the clans.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Grey as your beard. Lift your end.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The Wall was cut from this face. My grandsire's mark is on it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Three new houses in {town} want ashlar. Work all summer.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Work all summer, cough all winter.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bind a wet cloth round your mouth. Keeps the dust out.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ludham rebuilt in stone after the raid. Paid Sunward lenders for it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Stone won't burn. Debt won't either. Both last forever.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Better a debt than a cinder.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Mallet's head is cracked.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Take it to the smith tomorrow. Tonight I want ale.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ale and a soft seat. My arse is all grit.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Something's watching from the scree.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Goat. Or a Reaver scout pretending to be one.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Keep your crowbar close, either way.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ditching again. Third day of mud to the knees.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's a penny a day. Mud's free.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Everything's free when you've nothing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Robin's gone east. Says the Crows feed you and pay.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And hang you when the hero comes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Starving's slower. That's all it's got going for it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nobody's hiring. Not even for muck-spreading.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Stand by the cooper's. He shouts when his boy's drunk.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: His boy's always drunk. Good.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Two masters wanted me this morning. Two!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Don't get proud. Thriving towns forget fast.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Let me be proud till Friday.

who: two thieves on the night streets

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Watch passes the well every quarter hour. Count it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I'm counting. You're breathing too loud.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I've a cold. Thieves get colds same as honest folk.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Dark moon. Good night for work.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Slavers' favourite night too. Half the hamlets sleep in towers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then the town's softer. Every cloud, eh?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Chandler's shutter's got a loose pin.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Candles aren't worth the risk. Too bulky.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's the coin box behind them I'm after.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nothing in any larder. Not even rats.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then go for the granary. That's where the food is.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's where the guards are. I like my neck.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Watch is doubled. They're hunting {player}, not us.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Doubled watch catches anyone. Lie low tonight.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Shame. Busy guards make sloppy guards.

who: two thieves eyeing the market stalls

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Goldsmith keeps his key on a cord round his neck.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And his wife keeps the spare in her apron. I watched.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You've an eye for aprons, I'll give you that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Who's busy, who's lazy? Tell me.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The cloth man counts twice. The spicer naps after dinner.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Spicer, then. Pepper's worth more than silver, weight for weight.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sunward shops have locks on locks.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And guards with crossbows. Rich town, rich gaol.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Let's go back to Reedwatch. They don't even bolt doors.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fat market today. Purses swinging everywhere.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not today. Fat markets have the steward's men walking.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Tomorrow, then, when they've drunk their wages.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Turn it, turn it. You're letting it sag.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: My arms ache. Glass doesn't care about arms.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Neither do I. Turn it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Natron's come in from the flats. Good and white.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: White natron, clear glass. Grey natron, green glass.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Grey's what scares me. Too much grey salt in the world.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Heard of the Glass Serpent? Leaves the ground glassy behind it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then it's stealing our trade. Furnace-work for free.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You'd joke on your own pyre.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lady wants six goblets, all matched.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Six matched. Glass doesn't match. Glass is a mood.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then put it in a better mood. She pays well.

who: two salters raking the natron flats

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Rake it into rows. Sun does the rest.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sun does my head in, too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wet your hood at the pan. And stop moaning.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Natron's thick this year. Glassmen will pay double.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the fullers. And the curers. Salt of the desert.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Salt of my blisters, more like.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: See that patch? Grey. Not white. Grey.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Don't touch it. That's how the grey salt started, men say.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Salters found it first. We'll be blamed first too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Natron price is down. Too many rakers.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Too many hungry folk with rakes. Same thing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Dame Matilda's buyers pay more for the grey. Just saying.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Cover the rows. Dew'll melt it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Dew in the desert. My father never believed it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Your father never raked a flat. Cover them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Riders on the ridge. Dust Riders?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They want horses, not natron. Keep raking.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Keep raking slowly. Look poor.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Keep your eyes on the ridges, not the mule's arse.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The mule's arse doesn't shoot arrows at me.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Give it time. It's a Sunward mule.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Heard about the ambush on the grain road?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Escort ran, they say. I'd have run.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You'd have run first, with my bow.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Master paid somebody at the last ford. Saw the purse go.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Reavers' toll. Cheaper than burying us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then why are we here at all?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fire's too big. You can see it from three hills.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Cold's worse than outlaws.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Not if the outlaws bring knives.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Robert atte Green rides with us to the mesa.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we'll be fine. Outlaws know his name.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Outlaws know his price, too. That's the worry.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Heavy at the front, light at the back. Or she tips.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I've loaded carts since I was knee-high.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And tipped one every year since.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Rope's frayed. That'll snap on the first rut.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Rope costs. {steward} won't pay for new.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He'll pay for the lost load instead. Steward's sums.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Radham lost a whole cart last week. Thornbacks took it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Escort sold the route, they say.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then we don't tell the escort our road till we're on it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Third cart today. Grain everywhere.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Grain everywhere and my back nowhere.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Load it, moan later. That's the carter's oath.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Grain to {town} before the gates get busy.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oxen are stiff. Give them a minute.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Give me a minute too. I'm stiffer than they are.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Half a load. That's all the hamlet would give up.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They're hiding the rest. Can't blame them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The steward will. He'll call it rebellion.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Garrison's sending men with us this time.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Spears behind us. Feels like a funeral.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Better a funeral escort than a funeral.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sign here, or make your mark.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: My mark's a cross. Same as the last fellow's.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good enough. Crosses don't lie.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Kitchen door, not the front. They'll set the dogs on us.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Even the dogs eat better than we do here.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hush. The cook can hear through stone.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Two barrels for the innkeeper. Where's he want them?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Cellar. Mind the step, it's rotten.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Everything here is rotten. Except the ale, lucky.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We made it. I didn't think we'd make it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Saw a man on the road watching us. Never moved.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Scout. They'll take the next cart instead. Poor sods.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He says he'll pay at month's end.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: He said that last month.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then we take the load back. No coin, no {good}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Cloth for the hall. Sir Thomas's own order.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Honest lord, slow payer.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Honest and slow beats quick and crooked.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Last drop of the day. Then ale.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You've said 'then ale' at every stop.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And every stop I've meant it more.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Chain it twice. That oak's got a mind of its own.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oak's got more sense than this horse.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The horse can hear you, you know.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sawmill wants six trunks by Thursday.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Market day. They'll sell planks before the sap's dry.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Green planks warp. Not our problem.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wolf tracks in the ride. Fresh.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we haul faster. Wolves don't like noise.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Neither do I, but I'll shout if it helps.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wood for the town and no bread for us.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Burn some of it in our own hearth. Nobody counts bark.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The steward counts bark. He counts everything.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Leave the last log. Sun's going.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Charcoalers will have it by morning.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Charcoalers see everything at night. They'll see who took it.

who: two joiners' men fetching timber from the yard

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Seasoned oak, not that green rubbish.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The green's cheaper. Master said cheap.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Master said cheap. He didn't say crooked.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Everyone's building. Yard's half empty.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Take what's left before the masons grab it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Masons with timber. Next they'll want to thatch.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Burned hamlet wants roof beams. Lots of them.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Burnt once, they'll want them cheap.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Charge them fair. Could be us next.

who: two builders at work on a wall

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Plumb line says it leans.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Plumb line's drunk. The wall's fine.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The wall will be fine on the ground, too, soon.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: New houses all along the lane. Town's growing.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Growing towns need walls. Walls need us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And walls need paying for. Don't count your coin yet.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Palisade first, then the houses. That's the order.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The raiders came through the gap by the well.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then the gap's where we start. Sharpen those stakes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The lord wants the tower two courses higher.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Two courses of stone, ten of excuses from the quarry.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Just stack what we have. Then shout for more.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Blight-born came out of the dark at Dunworth. Walls didn't stop them.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Walls stop men. Nothing stops those.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then build it anyway. Folk sleep better behind stone.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Mortar's thin. They've cut it with sand.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They've cut our pay with sand too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Thin wall, thin pay, thin soup. Sounds right.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Frost in the mortar. Can't lay a course till noon.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we cut stone instead. No idle hands.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My hands are idle because they're frozen.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Every stone here's set dry. No mortar on the old Wall.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Stewards built it. Knew a thing or two.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Knew to cut stone straight, which is more than you do.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pass the spars. Twisted hazel, not straight.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Straight's easier to split.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And easier to pull out in a gale. Twisted.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fen reed lasts sixty years. Straw lasts twenty.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: This roof won't see sixty. Nor will we.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then thatch it for your grandsons.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Comb it down. It's lumpy at the eave.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's a roof, not a lady's hair.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lumpy thatch holds rain. Comb it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: First thing the raiders do is fire the thatch.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So lime-wash it. Slows the burn.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Slows it enough to get the children out. That's something.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Patching, not new. Nobody's got coin for new.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Patch over patch. The roof's a quilt.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A quilt that leaks on the baby. Tell her that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Careful, that crate clinks.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Clinks how? Glass or coin?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Neither of your business. Lift.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Stack the {good} by the stall. Not in the mud.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mud's everywhere. The stall's in the mud.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then on the boards. Use your eyes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Cart came in with an arrow in the tailboard.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Carter's white as milk. Won't say a word.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Let him be. He'll talk at the inn tonight.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Is that all? Four sacks for the whole town?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Four sacks and a lot of pleading.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Guard them. There'll be fists over these.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Last one. Then the oxen can rest.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the carter can drink.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And we can sit. Sitting's my favourite trade.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Take a third of a patch and leave the rest.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Like the lodges' Half Law, but for weeds.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They're not weeds if they cure you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The best herbs grow up on the butte-tops.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the best falls happen on the way up.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Reagent seekers climb it barefoot. You've got boots.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Don't pick near the grey ground. Leaves come up wrong.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wrong how?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Spotted. Bitter. Even the goats won't touch them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Herbs sell better than bread these days.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sick folk pay. Hungry folk can't.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sick and hungry folk just die. Pick faster.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Rowan twig, red thread, bound in a cross. Simple.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Simple sells. Folk don't trust a charm they understand.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then mutter over it. They like the muttering.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Everyone wants Blight charms now. Silver bells, salt bags.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Salt. They want salt, with grey salt in the world?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: White salt. I check it twice.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fever charm for a penny. Love charm for two.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Why's love dearer?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fever passes on its own. Love needs help.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Don't sell them here. The priest's watching.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: His own mother bought one last week.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then he can watch her, not us.

who: two gardeners in the physic garden

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sage by the wall, rue by the gate. Keep them apart.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Why? They're not feuding.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Rue spoils sage. Old rule. Mind it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Brother says the hyssop's for the altar, not the sick.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then the sick can pray for it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hush. Cut a little from the back where he won't see.

lines.text: Then you'll sleep soundly near them. It works.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Valerian for the widow. She can't sleep since the raid.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Root steeped in wine. Just a little.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A little, aye. Too much and she won't wake.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Cats roll in it like it's catnip.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Rats come to it too, they say.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then hang it high, or the house will be a fair.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yew stave, heart on the inside, sap on the back.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I know where the sap goes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then why's it on the wrong side?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Tiller it slow. Too fast and she'll crack.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Like a mule. Or a wife.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Or a bowyer's patience. Slow.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lord wants fifty bows for the levy.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fifty! Yew doesn't grow that fast.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Elm then. Better than sticks.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Best yew grows in the churchyard.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the priest guards it like gold.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bring him a bow for his nephew. He'll soften.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Grey goose for the fletching. Left wing feathers only.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What's wrong with right wing?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Spins the wrong way. Ask any archer.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Guards bought three sheaves. Cart road's got bad again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Bodkins or broadheads?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bodkins. Outlaws wear mail now, some of them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Glue's not set. Leave them overnight.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hide glue stinks like the tannery.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Everything that works stinks. Ask the fullers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Scrape with the grain, not against.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: My arms are dead from scraping.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Dead arms, live hide. Keep at it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Blackwater Men buy our leather by the cartload.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: To smuggle what?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Don't ask what. Ask how much.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Tallow and fish oil, rubbed in hot.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I'll smell of fish for a week.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You smelled of fish before this.

who: two charcoal burners at the clamp

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Smoke's gone blue. Close the vents.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Blue means she's nearly done?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Blue means she's burning the charcoal. Close them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Torches on the far ridge. Moving fast.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Outlaws or the lord's men?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Either way, we saw nothing. Charcoalers never see anything.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Smelters in Stonepass want ten loads.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we'll need ten clamps. Three nights each.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And no sleep for a month. Charcoal's life.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Turf's split on the windward side. Patch it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: If she flares, we lose a week's work.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Patch it, then. Stop talking.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sour as a steward's smile.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Press them for verjuice. Cooks pay for it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And a bit for sprains. Rub it in cold.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Throw the peel over your shoulder. It spells your lover's letter.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mine spelled a squiggle.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then you'll marry a squiggle.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Crab apples and honey. Almost a meal.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No honey left.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then crab apples and a long face. Still something.

who: two gatherers picking jelly ear off the elder

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jelly ear. Grows on elder, feels like a cold ear.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Ugh. It wobbles.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Boiled in milk, it soothes a sore throat. Wobble and all.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Judas ear, the priest calls it. Says Judas hanged himself on an elder.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's why they grow there?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That and the damp. I trust the damp more.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Dried, they keep all winter. Swell up again in soup.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Who buys these?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sunward cooks. They'll buy anything strange.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sell your coat and buy betony, my gran said.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: For what?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: For headaches, wounds, bad dreams. For everything.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Grows thick round the churchyard.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Folk plant it there to keep the dead resting.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then pick it gently. Don't wake anyone.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wear a sprig round your neck against evil spirits.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Will it keep off a Horror?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No. It'll keep off your worry, maybe.

who: two tower wardens inspecting the lookouts

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Beacon wood's damp at the base. Restack it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nobody's lit a beacon in anger for years.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then they'll light this one wet. Restack it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: John Hobson logs every lighting. Every night.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nobody reads his logbook.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Someone will, one day. Light it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Henry Black says he saw ash-light from tower four.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Henry drinks.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Henry drinks because he saw it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Stair's rotten on the third flight.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Write it for {steward}. He'll ignore it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Write it twice, then. He'll ignore it twice.

who: two outlaws of a band on a raid

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Grain and goats, nothing else. Don't burn the place.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: King said burn the barn.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: King's not here. My cousin's wife lives down there.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Blades blackened? Faces too?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Soot from the cook's fire. I smell like a hearth.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good. You'll pass for a Coldhearth.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Camp's hungry. Take the sacks, leave the people.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And if they fight?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They won't. They're hungry too. Just quicker about it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hero broke our other camp. Uncle's limping back.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we take double tonight. For him.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: For the Leans. For all of us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Thomas the Lean says leave the lord's carts alone.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Walter Crowfoot didn't. Look at him now. Rich.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Look at him now. Hunted. Pick your king careful.

who: two outlaws lying in wait by the road

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Keep down. Your hood sticks up like a hare's ear.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's cold, and my knees are wet.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wet knees beat a rope. Down.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Cart's coming. Two oxen, one guard.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: One guard? That's either luck or a trap.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Halfpennies don't believe in luck. Watch the treeline.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can't see past the next bend.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Neither can they. That's the point.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Clever. Your mam always said you were the clever Shortknife.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Garrison spears riding with the grain now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then let it pass. We take the one after.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The one after's ours. Pass the word down the line.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Two days on this bank and nothing but pedlars.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Rob a pedlar, then.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pedlars carry news and needles. Can't eat either.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Go-between says a sealed cart comes Friday.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Lord's seal? Thornback'd want it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then we take the seal and leave the grain for the hamlet.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There. Lone rider, good horse.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Herald's colours. Leave him.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Aye. Kill a herald and every lord comes hunting.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Word is a hero's out after camps like ours.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we're three roads away by noon.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My brother's in the next camp. I'll send him word.
